draft.title: Ways businesses reach customers
card: Businesses need ways to reach their customers. They can sell in a shopping centre, at a market, in a small local store, in a remote community store or online.
many shops under one roof, so customers can visit lots of businesses in one trip.
a place where many sellers set up stalls, often on certain days.
customers browse and buy using a website or app, and the goods are delivered.
draft.remember: Businesses choose a way to reach customers, such as a centre, market, local store, remote store or online.

a.q: Priya makes candles and sells them on a website. Customers order them and they are posted. How does she reach customers?
a.why: Customers buy through a website and the candles are posted, so she sells online. A market needs stalls where buyers visit in person, and Priya does not use one.
a.clue: Where do customers place their orders?

b.q: Sam sells fresh fruit from a stall on Saturday mornings in Alice Springs, alongside many other sellers. Which way is this?
b.why: A stall among many sellers on set days is a market. A shopping centre is a group of shops under one roof, not stalls, so it is the tempting wrong choice.

problems.detail: The card names five ways but explains only three. Small local stores and remote community stores are never described, yet 'remote community store' is used as a distractor in both questions.

Setting the stall in Alice Springs, a town some students may see as remote, makes the undefined 'remote community store' option seem plausible. Students cannot rule it out from the card, even though the stall-among-many-sellers detail points clearly to a market.

check.summary: Both questions have clear, correct answers (Online; A market). The card leaves small local stores and remote community stores undefined, and the Alice Springs setting in question b could make the undefined remote community store option tempting.

proposal.title: Ways businesses reach customers
card: Businesses need ways to reach their customers. A shopping centre has many shops under one roof, so people can visit lots of businesses in one trip.
A market is a place where many sellers set up stalls, often on certain days. A small local store is a single shop in a suburb or town that serves people living nearby, such as a corner shop.
A remote community store is a shop in a small community far from big towns. It is often the only shop there, so it sells food, clothes and other goods in one place.
Online, customers browse and buy using a website or app, and the goods are delivered to them.
proposal.remember: Businesses can reach customers through shopping centres, markets, local stores, remote community stores or online.

a.q: Priya makes candles and sells them on a website. Customers order them and they are posted. How does she reach customers?
a.why: Customers buy through a website and the candles are delivered by post, so she sells online. A market needs a stall where buyers visit in person, and Priya does not use one.
a.clue: Where do customers place their orders?

b.q: Leo runs a corner shop in a Hobart suburb. People who live nearby walk in to buy milk and bread. Which way is this?
b.why: A single shop in a suburb that serves nearby residents is a small local store. A remote community store is in a small community far from big towns, and a Hobart suburb is not like that.
b.clue: Is this one shop or many, and is it far from a town?
